blocks.text: Organizing your inbox for multiple estates

When you manage multiple estates, your inbox is your most important workspace. You should create a folder hierarchy that mirrors your physical filing system. Right-click your inbox and select New Folder for each estate. Name them clearly, perhaps using the estate name or the primary beneficiary. This keeps your active discussions separate from archived matters.
Using rules to automate your workflow

Automation is essential for keeping your focus on high-value tasks. Navigate to Tools > Rules > Edit Rules. You can set up a rule that looks for specific keywords in the subject line. If an email contains the estate name, have Outlook move it directly into the corresponding folder. This prevents incoming mail from cluttering your main view while you work on other matters.

items: ⌘ + N: Compose a new email message.
⌘ + Return: Send the current email message.
⌘ + R: Reply to the selected email.

blocks.text: Estate administration is deadline-driven. Do not rely on your memory for court dates or tax filing deadlines. Open your Calendar view with ⌘ + 2. Create an event for every milestone. Use the Reminder feature to trigger a notification three days before a filing is due. This gives you time to review documents and coordinate with beneficiaries.
If you struggle to find a specific setting, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item or button you need.

blocks.text: Common mistakes in Outlook for Mac

items: Ignoring the Focused Inbox: If you miss important emails, turn off Focused Inbox via View > Focused Inbox.
Forgetting to back up: Ensure your OLM files are backed up regularly if you use local storage.
Over-relying on search: Use advanced filters to find emails by sender or date range instead of simple keyword searches.
Using outdated versions: Ensure you are on macOS 14 or later to receive critical security updates for Outlook.

blocks.text: Communication with beneficiaries must be clear, professional, and consistent. Use the dictation feature to draft your initial thoughts quickly. Hold the fn key and speak your message. You can then polish the text before sending. This is faster than typing long updates about estate status.

Legal documents and financial statements are often large. If you need to send files that exceed your server limits, use a cloud storage link instead of attaching the file directly. Upload the document to your secure cloud drive, then paste the link into your email. This ensures the recipient can access the file without causing delivery errors.

faq.question: Can I use Outlook for Mac to manage my tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, Outlook for Mac has a built-in Tasks view. You can create tasks for estate follow-ups and assign them due dates to stay organized.

faq.question: Is Legacy Outlook still supported?
faq.answer: Support for Legacy Outlook for Mac with Exchange Online mailboxes is scheduled to end in October 2026. It is best to transition to the New Outlook interface now.

faq.question: How do I find a specific email from a beneficiary?
faq.answer: Use the search bar at the top of the app. You can click the filter icon to narrow your search by sender, date, or whether the email has attachments.
